thought.text: `devise :database_authenticatable` is there, so I'll use the class-level `authenticate`:

reasoning_content: Custom's user has `devise :database_authenticatable` — meaning `authenticate` should exist as a class method (that's the `authenticate_for_database` method… actually `User.authenticate` is defined by database_authenticatable). But the instance `u.authenticate` isn't defined — that's normal, Devise's `authenticate` is a class method. Let's use `User.authenticate(email, password)` (a class method that takes an email parameter) — Devise's database_authenticatable defines `def self.authenticate(credential, password)`.

action.command: cd /workspace && export PATH=/usr/local/ruby/bin:$PATH PGPASSWORD=root && timeout 200 bin/rails runner 'puts "authenticate admin: " + (User.authenticate("admin@consul.dev", "Aa12345678") ? "SUCCESS" : "FAIL"); puts "role users: " + %w[mod@consul.dev manager@consul.dev valuator@consul.dev verified@consul.dev unverified@consul.dev].map { |e| e.split("@").first + "=" + User.where(email: e).count.to_s }.join(", ")' 2>&1 | tail -3
